venue_vintage.health_center_rule: permanent, service delivery (not administrative-only), open 20+ hours a week, not a hospital, school, nursing home, shelter or correctional setting

observed.median_cv_label: standard error as a share of the estimate (the margin of error is 1.645 times this), tracts reporting 50 or more

national.tiers_label: mean and 5th-95th percentile of the draws: sampling and model noise given the model choices, not the range of the claim
not_modelled: household income as Medicaid and premium credits define it (the tiers use the survey's income-to-poverty ratio)
immigration status beyond the noncitizen carve-out

tracts.can_be_ranked_label: eligible people per resident, a different quantity from the adults-at-or-below-138% shares below

rankable_adults_le138.note: the model ranks fewer tracts on purpose: it will not rank noise

county_pools.scope: HealthCare.gov states only; state-run exchanges, Connecticut included, are not in the file

covers.rule: the 300 counties with the most tracts among those with 8 or more candidate venues

lead.text: expected reach of the optimiser's five sites against the five highest direct counts, same reach rule

A_holdout.rule: 20% of tracts with 3,000+ people withheld at random and refit
A_holdout.what_it_tests: the prediction against the survey's own count, which is noisy; the noise is simulated from the model's own weight function

A_holdout_all_sizes.rule: 20% of tracts of any size withheld at random and refit
A_holdout_all_sizes.what_it_tests: the same, including the small tracts that the 3,000+ rule leaves out

B_sahie_independent_refit.what_it_tests: a refit without SAHIE, summed to counties. It is calibrated to ACS county totals, so it mostly tests the ACS against SAHIE (administrative records). The log-count correlation is driven by county size; the rate gap is the useful number.

D_simulation.what_it_tests: a simulation inside the model: truth is drawn from the fitted model, so these are results for a world the model describes, not for the real one. The split at 100% of poverty and the share of children at 400% and over are held fixed in it.

rankable_adults_le138.note: the model ranks fewer tracts on purpose: it will not rank noise

E2_browser_interval.note: the factor is for the default settings; other settings are approximate

F_scenarios.plan_selection_slider: 0 to +30% on the eligible pool; a scenario, not a forecast

validation.not_run: validation C (replication on the 2015-2019 survey) and a binomial-logit interval-width check

methods.sahie_benchmark: scale to the nearest edge of SAHIE's 90% interval when the county mean is outside it

example_county.label: Comal County, TX
example_county.rule: the median-population county among those in states that have not expanded Medicaid (so the coverage gap is not zero) with 8 or more candidate venues

open_enrollment.text: HealthCare.gov: enroll by Dec 15 for Jan 1 coverage; open until Jan 15.
open_enrollment.state_text: runs its own marketplace, with its own dates.

state_marketplaces.note: These states enroll people on their own sites, with their own deadlines, so the page shows no HealthCare.gov dates for them. The other states use HealthCare.gov.

effectuated_enrollment.note: Cited, not recomputed. KFF published 2026-07-28 from CMS monthly effectuated enrollment data (as of 2026-05-05 for 2026).

immigrant_eligibility.note: From 2027 certain other lawfully present immigrants lose premium tax credit eligibility. The KFF FAQ does not list the groups, so neither does this analysis. Noncitizen adults are a separate tier labelled 'eligibility varies'.

waiver_flags.WI: BadgerCare Plus covers adults to 100% of poverty under a waiver

tier_rules.medicaid_range: Adults 19 to 64 at or below 138% of poverty in expansion states (bands under 1.00 and 1.00 to 1.37). In Wisconsin, adults under 100% are placed here and flagged.
tier_rules.coverage_gap: Adults 19 to 64 under 100% of poverty in the other non-expansion states, Georgia included (its Pathways program has a work requirement and small enrollment).
tier_rules.subsidy_range: Adults 138% to 399% of poverty in expansion states; 100% to 399% in non-expansion states.
tier_rules.d400: People at 400% of poverty and over, adults and children: full price, no premium credit for adults, and most children are above the Medicaid and CHIP limits.
tier_rules.children: Under 19 and under 400% of poverty: most are eligible for Medicaid or CHIP; the income limit varies by state. Children at 400% and over are in the 400% tier.
tier_rules.noncitizen: Noncitizen adults are carved out of every adult tier. The survey cannot tell green card holders from other noncitizens.

federal_law_2027.work_requirements: From 2027-01-01, expansion-state Medicaid adults to age 64 must show work or similar activity (80 hours a month) unless exempt; HHS can let a state wait until no later than 2028-12-31 if it shows a good-faith effort. Not modelled here: the tiers use income only.
federal_law_2027.immigrants: Federal law limits Medicaid for some lawfully present immigrants from 2026-10-01 and premium tax credits for some from 2027-01-01. The groups are not modelled: noncitizen adults are their own tier, 'eligibility varies'.

not_modelled: household income as Medicaid and premium credits define it (the tiers use the survey's income-to-poverty ratio)
